name: Eight hours target / 'sleep is looksmaxxing'

lead: This is the belief that sleep comes first among looksmaxxing habits, usually with an eight-hour goal.
Public guidance recommends roughly 7 to 9 hours for adults.

paras: Proponents say adequate sleep avoids visible signs such as eye bags.[1]
Habitual short sleep is associated with chronic health conditions.[1]

lead: The phrase 'sleep is looksmaxxing' expresses the view in appearance communities that adequate sleep is the most basic appearance improvement, often with a target of about eight hours a night.

Guidance cited on Wikipedia varies: the US National Sleep Foundation recommends about 7 hours for adults, with other cited ranges of 7 to 9 hours for ages 18 to 64.[1] Sleep deprivation is associated with eye bags, puffiness, weight gain and other effects.[1]

paras: The National Sleep Foundation recommends about 7 hours per night for adults, and cited guidance gives 7 to 9 hours for ages 18 to 64; adults sleeping under seven hours are more likely to have chronic conditions.[1]
No studies found on sleep duration as an appearance intervention in the sources consulted.
